title: Projected service account token for a non-Kubernetes API
summary: The kubelet mounts a short-lived, audience-bound service account token into the pod. Another service verifies it against the cluster's OIDC issuer, so no shared secret is needed.
notes: Projected tokens expire (e.g. after 1 hour) and the kubelet refreshes them before they do. The legacy Secret-based tokens never expired and are no longer created automatically.
Set a specific audience (e.g. 'payments-api'). The receiving service rejects tokens meant for anyone else, so a stolen token can't be replayed against the Kubernetes API or a different service.
The receiver validates the signature with the issuer's public keys (/.well-known/openid-configuration and JWKS), or calls the TokenReview API if it can reach the cluster.
This is the building block under AKS Workload Identity, EKS IRSA and GKE Workload Identity Federation: the same token, trusted by a cloud instead of your own service.

nodes.label: Cluster service account issuer
nodes.description: Publishes OIDC discovery and JWKS so outside services can verify tokens.
